claims.statement: The server's only transport is StdioServerTransport: it is imported in the entry point and instantiated exactly once after every tool and prompt registration, so the process serves a single client session over stdin/stdout with no HTTP, SSE, port, URL or session-header alternative.

stdout carries JSON-RPC traffic only by construction: no code under src/ calls console.log or writes to process.stdout, and every operator-facing message (auto-detection notice, startup banner, warnings, debug dumps, tool registration failures) is emitted through console.error, making stderr the diagnostic channel.

The --debug flag (and NODEMW_MCP_DEBUG=1) is forwarded into the nodemw client options, which activates third-party logging inside the same process that owns the protocol channel and therefore places verbose debugging in tension with a clean stdout JSON-RPC stream.

Process-wide state — the Bot instance, the stored ServerConfig, and the authenticated flag — lives in module-level singletons, and getBot() throws rather than constructing a client on demand; combined with a target wiki resolved once during argument parsing, this forces a one-process-per-wiki-target, one-client-per-process mapping with no runtime re-pointing.

createServer constructs the McpServer with a constant name 'nodemw-mcp-server', the version imported from package.json, the description 'MediaWiki API bridge for AI agents', a declared capabilities object containing only tools, and the caller-supplied description as the instructions field; it holds no wiki-specific knowledge itself.

The capabilities a client actually receives are the SDK-merged union of the declared tools fragment and the fragments contributed by handler registration, yielding tools with listChanged plus prompts with listChanged, while resources, logging, completions, sampling, and tasks are never advertised or backed by handlers.

Prompt support exists only because the operating-principles prompt is registered: the explicit capability literal lists tools alone, so removing that registration would drop the prompts capability from the handshake as well as the prompt from prompts/list.

The MCP catalog is immutable for the process lifetime: all tools and the prompt are registered before server.connect, the SDK refuses capability registration once a transport is attached, and no tools/list_changed or prompts/list_changed notification is ever emitted despite listChanged being advertised.

Authentication state changes the contents of tools/list, not the advertised capabilities: guest registration skips the write registrar array (37 read-only tools) while an authenticated session concatenates it (54 tools), so write availability can be read from the tool count or the instructions auth line but never from capabilities.

The instructions field is the primary channel carrying agent-facing runtime context: one generated string supplies sitename, MediaWiki version, main page, api.php endpoint, language instruction, site statistics, auth status (username, groups, key rights, or a GUEST warning), and a static operating-principles block separated by a delimiter line, and that same string is also returned verbatim (prefixed with 'Read and follow these rules:') by the operating-principles prompt for clients that do not auto-inject instructions.

The .mcp.json in the repository working copy is a single-entry local wiring sample (command node, args ["dist/index.js"], env carrying plaintext NODEMW_MCP_SERVER, NODEMW_MCP_MW_USER and NODEMW_MCP_MW_PASS values) that .gitignore itself ignores alongside config.json, so it is neither something a clone receives nor a shareable template; and because the args path is relative and dist/ is gitignored, it only works after a build has produced dist/index.js.

The published-package wiring shape ('npx @xiedada/nodemw-mcp-server') is supported by package.json mapping the nodemw-mcp-server bin and main to dist/index.js, shipping only dist in the tarball, and requiring Node.js 18 or newer.

Client configuration is read only inside parseCliArgs, which merges each setting as flag-before-env across seven NODEMW_MCP_* variables, so flags placed in a host's args array override an env block and any configuration change requires respawning the process.

NODEMW_MCP_MW_TOKEN is documented in both README environment tables but no code path reads it, and the --token flag it is documented as equivalent to is parsed into config.token yet never forwarded to the nodemw client, so token-only wiring yields a silent guest session with all write tools hidden.

Startup failure semantics are asymmetric from the client's perspective: the four checkpoints inside main() (missing target server, API path auto-detection, login, site-info/statistics fetch) print a message to stderr and call process.exit(1), whereas anything after them falls through main().catch(console.error), which logs the raw error without setting a non-zero exit code.

Every tool-call failure reaches the client as an ordinary CallToolResult with isError true rather than as a JSON-RPC error response: wiki-level failures are wrapped by the tool wrappers' own errorResult, while the SDK's tools/call handler catches all other throws — unknown tool name, input validation failure, output validation failure, handler exception — into an isError result, so a host that only surfaces protocol errors looks like it is silently succeeding.

The server presents two distinct identities: the constant serverInfo name for host UIs, and a DEFAULT_USER_AGENT sent to the wiki that composes nodemw, Node.js, platform/architecture, package, and MCP SDK versions, which --user-agent replaces outright and --user-agent-append extends instead.

The protocol surface has automated coverage only at the server-object level: annotations.test.ts, smoke.test.ts and readGuard.test.ts wire an McpServer to the SDK Client over InMemoryTransport.createLinkedPair(), so tools/list and tools/call are exercised without stdio, while test-server.js still only spawns node dist/index.js, waits about two seconds and dumps the captured streams without ever writing a JSON-RPC frame.

The initialize response is assembled by the SDK rather than by repository code: protocolVersion echoes the client's requested version when it is one of the supported versions (2025-11-25, 2025-06-18, 2025-03-26, 2024-11-05, 2024-10-07) and otherwise falls back to the latest, serverInfo and capabilities come from the createServer arguments, and instructions is included only when the string is non-empty.

The stdio wire format is newline-delimited JSON: each message is serialized as one line of JSON.stringify plus a newline and the reader splits the buffer on newlines before parsing, with no Content-Length style header, so a host, proxy, or wrapper that reframes the stream or merges lines makes the peer unable to deserialize messages.

The child process has no graceful shutdown or reconnection path of its own — src installs no SIGINT/SIGTERM handler and never calls server.close() or transport.close() — and the SDK stdio transport only subscribes to stdin data and error events, never end, so closing the host's write side does not terminate the session; the process lives until the host kills it, and one process equals one session.

Protocol-level errors are silent on the server: the SDK forwards transport errors such as a malformed inbound JSON line only to an optional protocol onerror callback, and McpServer never registers one, so a bad frame is dropped with nothing written to stderr, which is a common reason a client sees no response while the server log stays empty.

Tool results travel on two channels that are not uniformly filled: 48 of the 54 tools declare an outputSchema and return jsonResult, which puts the same object into pretty-printed content text and structuredContent; get-article, get-article-by-revision and expand-templates always return a single text block and declare no schema, parse returns plain text by default and jsonResult only when include or limit_report is set, and get-module-source plus get-articles return structuredContent without declaring any schema; error results carry text only plus isError, so a client must read content text as the universal fallback and may use structuredContent as an optimization.

Because the SDK validates a non-error result against the tool's declared outputSchema, a success path that returns no structuredContent or mismatched structuredContent is rejected as an Output validation error and surfaces as an isError tool result for that single call only — not as a startup failure or a protocol fault.

Each tools/list entry carries title, annotations and an optional outputSchema, so a host can gate approvals from the catalog alone: all 37 read tools set readOnlyHint true, all 17 write tools set readOnlyHint false, and 15 of the 17 set destructiveHint true, with purge and undelete the two non-destructive exceptions.

A reconnect is a new process, so it resets everything the session accumulated: readState and writeCache are module-level Maps that die with the process, the login and its cookie jar are established once at startup, and the instructions string is assembled from startup probes before connect, so nothing in the protocol refreshes any of them mid-process.

The operating-principles block inside instructions states the reconnect contract to the model explicitly: that the server process is started fresh for every client connection including /mcp reconnects, that read-before-write state is per-connection so the target page must be re-read after any reconnect, and that a not-allowed or login-required write failure most likely means an expired login that requires a reconnect.

Authenticated sessions run a 60-second login heartbeat after connect: a meta=userinfo poll that, on positive anonymous evidence, flips the internal authenticated flag to false and prints a one-shot LOGIN SESSION EXPIRED banner on stderr instructing a /mcp reconnect, while leaving the already-registered write tools in place and never running at all for guest sessions.

main() installs a process-wide uncaughtException handler before any wiki work, logging a single '[nodemw-mcp] Suppressed uncaught exception in wiki response handling: …' line to stderr so that an unexpected response shape from a nodemw event-stack callback cannot kill the single-process session; the cost is that the affected tool call hangs until the client's own timeout.

The InMemoryTransport tests prove the server object is transport-agnostic but bypass createServer: they construct a bare McpServer with capabilities {tools:{}} and call registerAllTools directly, so instructions, the prompts capability, prompts/get, stdio framing and initialize version negotiation are never asserted, and the npm publish workflow runs npm ci and npm run build without running the test suite.

The published tarball contains only dist, so src, scripts and patches are not distributed: the nodemw patch is applied by postinstall patch-package only in a repository checkout, which means npx consumers run against the unpatched registry dependency and cannot assume the dependency-level hardening.

The READMEs document only the CLI, the environment variables and the tool list; neither mentions the instructions field nor the operating-principles prompt, so the delivery path of the behavior contract is discoverable only from source.
